questions.passage_text: For the following questions answer them individually
questions.question_text: What is the time complexity of searching an element in a binary search tree with n nodes in the worst case?
questions.solution_text: In the worst case, a binary search tree can degenerate into a linear structure (like a linked list) when all nodes are inserted in sorted order. In this case, searching requires traversing all n nodes, giving O(n) time complexity.
questions.full_markdown:
### Question

What is the time complexity of searching an element in a binary search tree with n nodes in the worst case?

**Options:**
- A. O(1)
- B. O(log n)
- C. O(n) ✅
- D. O(n log n)

questions.passage_text: For the following questions answer them individually
questions.question_text: In a relational database, which normal form eliminates transitive dependencies?
questions.solution_text: Third Normal Form (3NF) eliminates transitive dependencies. A relation is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on the primary key.
questions.full_markdown:
### Question

In a relational database, which normal form eliminates transitive dependencies?

**Options:**
- A. First Normal Form (1NF)
- B. Second Normal Form (2NF)
- C. Third Normal Form (3NF) ✅
- D. Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)

questions.passage_text: For the following questions answer them individually
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of object-oriented programming?
questions.solution_text: Goto statements are a feature of procedural programming and are generally discouraged in object-oriented programming. The main characteristics of OOP are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.
questions.full_markdown:
### Question

Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of object-oriented programming?

**Options:**
- A. Encapsulation
- B. Inheritance
- C. Polymorphism
- D. Goto statements ✅

questions.passage_text: For the following questions answer them individually
questions.question_text: What is the maximum number of comparisons required to sort an array of n elements using merge sort?
questions.solution_text: Merge sort has a time complexity of O(n log n) in all cases (best, average, and worst). It divides the array into two halves recursively (log n levels) and merges them (n comparisons at each level).
questions.full_markdown:
### Question

What is the maximum number of comparisons required to sort an array of n elements using merge sort?

**Options:**
- A. O(n)
- B. O(n log n) ✅
- C. O(n²)
- D. O(2ⁿ)

questions.passage_text: For the following questions answer them individually
questions.question_text: In the context of operating systems, what does 'thrashing' refer to?

options.label: A
options.option_text: CPU spending more time on scheduling than executing processes

options.label: B
options.option_text: Excessive page swapping between main memory and secondary storage

questions.solution_text: Thrashing occurs when the system spends most of its time swapping pages between main memory and secondary storage rather than executing processes. This happens when there are too many processes in memory relative to the available physical memory.
questions.full_markdown:
### Question

In the context of operating systems, what does 'thrashing' refer to?

**Options:**
- A. CPU spending more time on scheduling than executing processes
- B. Excessive page swapping between main memory and secondary storage ✅
- C. Deadlock between multiple processes
- D. Memory fragmentation issues
